review_type: Repository-owner-commissioned AI-assisted Econometrica numerical-methods advisory review
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not continue this cumulative manuscript through another ordinary revision round. A new, sharply focused paper on direct post-training neural Bellman certification for compact nonlinear control could merit evaluation, but the current evidence does not establish a method-specific Econometrica-level contribution for the broad NBO program.

independent_review_execution.execution_basis: The standard-library review audit was executed against the downloaded source-bound R41 publication artifact.

blocking_findings: R41 directly verifies four frozen nonlinear networks but does not establish a constructive or reliable nonlinear neural training method.

The contemporaneously reoptimized spline policy has strictly lower cost in fourteen of sixteen displayed comparisons, is never certified worse, and has tighter global and displayed-state policy bounds in all four economies.
There is no matched end-to-end work-to-certified-accuracy comparison; neural verification clocks exclude historical label construction and network training.
Adaptive precision is activated but is slower than fixed64 in every one of the twelve single-run matched objects and pays for forty-two rejected binary32 proposals.
The executed nonlinear problem remains scalar, four-date, three-shock, and grid-first; the multidimensional continuous-innovation theorem is not an executed scaling result.
The verified reoptimization gain is economically valid but method-neutral and is delivered more sharply by the conventional spline construction.
The nonzero implementation account is strong for the declared nearest-node scalar policy but does not close nonlinear training arithmetic or the broader NBO deployment pipelines.
The 68-page article, 45-page supplement, and 48-page applications companion retain a platform-level scope disproportionate to the completed method-specific evidence.
positive_findings: The stored current and future neural networks are now the direct Bellman objects; the certificate executes with the spline evaluator disabled.
The direct residual theorem appears internally coherent under its compact-domain, cover, terminal, and monotone-risk assumptions.
The precision catalogue genuinely exercises binary32 rejection, binary64 escalation, and mixed-precision services.
The nonlinear deployment account supplies a nonzero uniform binary32 arithmetic allowance.
Displayed-state neural regret is now below the verified reoptimization gain in the changed-price economies.
A contemporaneously reoptimized spline policy is reported and unfavorable comparisons are retained.
The failed R40 execution, source chronology, hashes, and active compilation diagnostics are preserved with unusually strong provenance.

limitations: The reviewer did not rerun neural training, the nonlinear verification catalogue, or the precision services; new runs would be new observations rather than verification of frozen clocks.
Single service clocks are descriptive and do not support hardware-general performance inference.
The reviewer checked the direct theorem chain, source-bound records, and selected implementation formulas, not every inherited theorem in the cumulative manuscript.
No claim is made that spline dominance extends beyond the four declared scalar economies or that fixed64 dominates all possible adaptive designs.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
